Operator: Good day, and welcome to the TeleWave Communications Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to request through the phone keypad by pressing star then one on your touchtone phone. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to TeleWave Communications' Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for the second quarter. We achieved solid revenue growth and robust subscriber additions, which reflects our strong execution in a dynamic market. We are particularly excited about the initial performance of our NexStream Ultra streaming service and its meaningful impact on ARPU uplift and cross-sell penetration. Our investments in network hardening and retention initiatives are also paying off, driving increased customer satisfaction and loyalty through lower churn across all segments. Furthermore, we have focused on disciplined cost management and operational efficiencies, which has allowed us to maintain strong profitability. Finally, our strategic focus remains on accelerating fiber deployments and converging our telecom infrastructure with premium media offerings to capture share in the multi-gig and 5G media era.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mike. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $5.2 billion, representing a 6% increase year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $1.93 billion, with a margin of 37.1%. We continue to manage our expenses effectively and are on track to meet our financial targets for the year. Our capital expenditures were $1.7 billion, primarily driven by investments in our 5G network expansion and fiber buildout.

Before I dive deeper into the segment results, I'd like to spend some time on one of our key growth drivers: our fiber buildout program. As you know, TeleWave has been aggressively expanding our FTTH – that's Fiber-to-the-Home – footprint as part of our 'Gigabit Everywhere' strategy, positioning us at the forefront of the broadband race against traditional cable MSOs like Comcast and Charter, as well as wireless alternatives from T-Mobile and Verizon.

In the second quarter, we achieved a major milestone by passing 1.2 million incremental homes, bringing our total homes passed to 18.5 million nationwide – up 28% year-over-year from 14.4 million at this time last year. This represents the strongest quarterly construction pace in our history, with us deploying over 22,000 route miles of fiber in the quarter alone. For context, that's equivalent to circling the Earth almost once. Our engineering teams, leveraging Nokia's next-gen 10G PON platforms and automated splicing technologies, reduced deployment costs by 15% quarter-over-quarter, down to approximately $850 per passing – well below the industry average of $1,100 cited in recent Dell'Oro Group reports.

Regionally, we're firing on all cylinders. In the Northeast, where we overlap with Verizon FiOS territory, we completed Phase 2 of our New England cluster, passing an additional 450,000 homes across urban nodes in Boston, Providence, and Hartford. This builds on our 2023 wins, where we captured 22% market share in direct FiOS overlap markets. In the Southeast, our greenfield push through the Carolinas and Georgia added 500,000 homes, fueled by $150 million in state-level matching grants under the federal BEAD program – that's the Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment initiative from the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act. We're now 85% through our initial BEAD-eligible footprint, with low-cost rural densification using micro-trenching techniques that cut permitting times by 40%.

Moving west to the Midwest and Mountain West, we accelerated in partnership with local co-ops, passing 250,000 homes in underserved markets like Omaha and Boise. Here, we're deploying symmetric multi-gigabit services up to 8Gbps downstream and 2Gbps upstream on our XGS-PON overlay, which supports not just residential broadband but also enterprise backhaul for our 5G small cells. Overall capex for fiber in Q2 came in at $1.1 billion, representing 65% of total capex, but with a forward guidance of flattening to $4.2-4.5 billion for full-year 2024 as we lap peak construction and shift toward maintenance mode.

Our homes passed growth isn't just about raw numbers – it's about high-value density. We've prioritized markets with take-rate potential above 30%, focusing on middle-mile aggregation to existing poles and ducts acquired from legacy providers. This quarter, we expanded coverage to 95% of our top 50 target MSAs, including full saturation in Atlanta and Charlotte. Looking ahead, we plan to pass another 4.5 million homes in the second half, with 1 million in overbuild scenarios against cable incumbents. This positions us to capture the ongoing cord-cutting boom, where streaming households – think Netflix, Disney+, and our own TeleWave Stream bundle – demand low-latency, high-reliability networks for 4K/8K video and cloud gaming.

A key technical initiative here is our rollout of DOCSIS 4.0 hybrid upgrades in legacy HFC territories as a bridge, but fiber remains the crown jewel. We've also integrated Open RAN elements for fixed-wireless augmentation in low-density areas, passing an effective 200,000 additional homes via mmWave overlays. Competitively, this puts us ahead of AT&T's slower fiber ramp – they're at about 1 million homes per quarter – and gives us leverage in wholesale deals, like our new dark fiber IRU agreements with hyperscalers for AI data center backhaul.

Finally, customer adoption – the real proof in the pudding. We added 285,000 fiber broadband subscribers in Q2, a 35% YoY increase, bringing our total fiber subs to 4.8 million – that's a 26% take rate on homes passed, up from 22% a year ago and accelerating sequentially from 24% in Q1. Residential take rates hit 28% in mature markets like the Northeast (where we've been live >24 months), rivaling Comcast's Xfinity Gigabit penetration. In newer builds, we're seeing 15-20% Day 1 uptake, driven by aggressive pricing: our 1Gig plan at $70/month with no data caps, bundling 500Mbps upload for remote work and Zoom warriors.

ARPU on fiber subs is shining at $118, up 8% YoY, thanks to upsell to 2Gig/5Gig tiers – now 22% of new adds – and video bundling with our 100+ channel TeleWave Media package, including Peacock and Paramount+ integrations. Churn remains elite at 0.9% monthly, half the industry average, as fiber customers stick due to superior Wi-Fi 7 gateways and our self-install app, which boosted activations by 25%.

Enterprise adoption is another tailwind: 45,000 new fiber-connected businesses, including SMBs migrating from DSL, with dedicated 10G Ethernet services growing 40% YoY. This diversifies revenue, with fiber enterprise now 18% of broadband mix.

Strategically, this buildout isn't just about broadband – it's a platform for media synergies. With fiber's low latency (<5ms), we're piloting PON-based delivery for live sports streaming in partnership with ESPN, targeting 2025 NFL season exclusivity in our footprint. We're also eyeing M&A tuck-ins, like potential rural ILECs, to hit 30 million homes passed by 2026 at a blended cost of $800/passing.

In summary, our fiber program is delivering: accelerating passes, rising take rates, and premium economics that will drive 15-18% broadband revenue growth this year. We're not just building pipe – we're building a defensible moat in the multi-gig era.

Good morning, everyone, and thanks for joining our Q2 earnings call. Today, I'd like to dive deep into our churn rate performance, a critical leading indicator for customer lifetime value and long-term revenue stability in our Telecommunications and Media segments. For context, we're reporting blended churn across our postpaid mobile, fixed broadband, and video/streaming services. Our overall monthly churn rate improved to 1.12% in Q2, down 15 basis points year-over-year from 1.27% and 8 basis points sequentially from Q1's 1.20%. On an annualized basis, this equates to approximately 13.2%, well below the industry average of 16-18% as reported by S&P Global for Tier 1 telcos like AT&T and Verizon.

Let me break this down by segment for clarity, using our standard 30-day rolling average methodology, which excludes voluntary downgrades and focuses on outright disconnections. Postpaid Mobile: Monthly churn held steady at a market-leading 0.85%, an improvement of 5 basis points YoY and flat QoQ. This represents about 45% of our total subscriber base, or 28 million lines. Family plan retention remains our strength, with churn under 0.70% for bundles including our 5G Unlimited Max tier—mirroring Verizon's success with premium plans but at a lower ARPU threshold of $58.

Fixed Broadband: Here we saw the most progress, with churn dropping to 1.05% monthly (down 25 bps YoY from 1.30%). This segment, powering 18 million households via our DOCSIS 4.0 and FTTH expansions, benefited from reduced outages post our $2.5 billion capex in network hardening. For comparison, Comcast's Xfinity broadband churn has hovered around 1.20% amid similar multi-gig upgrades.

Video/Streaming (including our StreamMax SVOD service): Churn ticked up slightly to 2.15% monthly (up 10 bps YoY), driven by seasonal content lulls and intensifying competition from Netflix and Disney+. This impacts our 12 million video subs, where cord-cutting pressures persist—our hybrid MVPD + OTT model lost 150K video subs net, aligning with broader industry trends where U.S. pay-TV households declined 3% per Nielsen data.

Over the past four quarters, we've achieved four straight quarters of YoY improvement: Q2 FY24 at 1.12% with -15 bps from network-led retention gains; Q1 FY24 at 1.20% with -10 bps from promotional bundling offsetting inflation; Q4 FY23 at 1.25% with -5 bps from holiday loyalty campaigns; Q3 FY23 at 1.30% baseline amid economic headwinds peak. This outpaces peers like T-Mobile (1.18% postpaid churn in their latest) and European incumbents like Vodafone (1.45% blended). Annualized, this has stabilized our subscriber base at 65 million total RGU's, adding $450 million in avoided revenue leakage.

Our proprietary churn attribution model, leveraging machine learning on 10+ petabytes of customer journey data, isolates these factors: Competitive Poaching accounts for 35% of churn, with aggressive pricing from MVNOs like Mint Mobile and cablecos' 5G Home Internet offers, including a 20% uptick in port-outs to Spectrum Mobile in the Midwest. Economic Sensitivity is 25%, with prepaid churn spiking to 3.2% monthly among lower-ARPU segments ($25/month), tied to 4.1% U.S. unemployment in Rust Belt states, though postpaid families were more resilient at 0.75%. Service Quality is 20%, where legacy copper/DSL migrations drove 15% of broadband churn early in Q2, now mitigated by 85% FTTH coverage in key markets. Content and Experience is 15%, with video churn correlating 0.75 with Netflix's password-sharing crackdown—our StreamMax saw 8% lift in trials but 12% drop-off post-free period, plus app crashes during live sports like the NBA Finals buffering. Other factors are 5%, including regulatory moves like the FCC's number porting rules and EU roaming caps.

Regionally: North America (85% of revenue) at 1.08% U.S. churn, strongest in Sunbelt states (0.95%) thanks to 5G Ultra Wideband rollout covering 75% of our footprint; Canada saw mild pressure at 1.25% from Rogers' merger synergies. Europe (10%) elevated at 1.45% due to price regulation in Germany and the UK's Ofcom-mandated mid-contract switches, but our Vodafone partnership JV helped cap this at 1.35% in the UK. Latin America (5%) prepaid-heavy at 2.80%, improving via Claro Brasil bundles—down 40 bps YoY on economic rebound.

We're not resting on this progress. Our "Zero Churn 2025" playbook includes an AI-Powered Retention Engine deployed to 90% of at-risk accounts, predicting churn 45 days out with 92% accuracy using XGBoost models on NPS, usage, and billing data, driving a 22% reduction in predicted churners via personalized offers like $10/month 5G discounts for high-usage gamers. Bundling 2.0 achieves 65% penetration of our "Total Connect" quad-play (mobile + broadband + video + IoT), cutting blended churn by 30% for adopters with ARPU uplift of $15 to $142, echoing Charter's success. Network Investments total $1.8 billion in Q3 for Open RAN and edge computing to slash latency below 10ms, targeting esports and cloud gaming demographics. Content Wars Counter includes exclusive StreamMax deals with Peacock and Paramount+ originals, plus ad-supported tiers at $5.99 to combat Netflix's 15% price hike backlash.

Looking ahead, we guide Q3 blended churn to 1.05-1.10%, assuming stable macros. If inflation eases and our 5G SA core launches on time, we see sub-1.00% by FY25—unlocking 2-3 points of EBITDA margin expansion. This positions us to gain share in a consolidating market, much like T-Mobile's postpaid gains post-Sprint.

As we turn to our profitability metrics, I'm pleased to report that our consolidated EBITDA margin came in at 37.2% for the quarter, up 120 basis points year-over-year and marking our strongest quarterly performance since the integration of our StreamLink media assets in 2022. This outperformance was driven by a 4% revenue growth across our core wireless and broadband segments, coupled with disciplined cost management amid moderating inflation pressures.

Looking ahead, we're guiding for Q3 2024 EBITDA margins in the range of 36.5% to 38.0%, reflecting seasonal headwinds from higher customer acquisition costs during promotional ramps for our 5G fixed wireless access offers, partially offset by accelerating synergies from our recently closed acquisition of an ad-tech platform. For the full fiscal year 2024, we now expect consolidated EBITDA margins of 37.0% to 38.5%, an upward revision of 50 basis points from our prior guide, underpinned by stronger-than-expected wireless service revenue growth and opex efficiencies.

On the revenue side, our mobile ARPU grew 2.8% year-over-year to $52.40, fueled by 5G Standalone core network deployments reaching 85% coverage in our top 50 U.S. metro markets—on par with AT&T's aggressive rollout but ahead of T-Mobile's in enterprise private 5G. We're seeing uptake in premium 5G plans bundled with our VeriStream+ service, which now boasts 12 million subscribers, up 25% YoY, thanks to exclusive NFL streaming rights and partnerships with Disney for ad-supported tiers. This bundling strategy is yielding a 15% higher lifetime value per sub compared to standalone wireless, mirroring successes at Charter's Spectrum bundle.

Regionally, North America remains our margin powerhouse at 40.1% for Q2, benefiting from fiber-to-the-x passings expanding 8% to nearly 20 million homes, with take rates hitting 26%. In Europe, margins held steady at 32.5%, despite regulatory headwinds from the EU's Digital Markets Act imposing content portability mandates; however, our Open RAN pilots in Germany and the UK are delivering 20% capex savings, positioning us for 200 bps expansion in H1 2025. APAC growth markets, including our Indonesian JV with Telkomsel, contributed 28% margins but high growth at 15% revenue CAGR from 5G mmWave spectrum wins in the recent auctions.

Cost levers are equally critical. We've realized $450 million in annual run-rate savings from network virtualization via our SDN/NFV stack, reducing transport opex by 12%—leveraging Ericsson's cloud-native solutions similar to those deployed by Verizon. AI-driven predictive maintenance on our edge compute infrastructure cut downtime 30%, directly flowing to EBITDA. Content costs, a drag at 22% of media revenues, are being mitigated through targeted FAST channel expansions (now 150+ channels) and dynamic ad insertion tech, boosting ad yield 18% to $25 CPM, in line with Roku's platform economics.

Strategically, we're prioritizing '5G Media Fusion'—integrating low-latency edge networks with AR/VR content delivery to capture the $50 billion immersive media TAM by 2028, per Gartner. This includes pilots for cloud gaming with Xbox, targeting 5 million users by YE2025. Headwinds to note: energy costs up 7% from data center expansions for AI workloads, and potential FCC spectrum repack costs in the U.S. post-C-band auctions. But with free cash flow conversion at 45% and net leverage at 2.1x, we have ample dry powder for $2-3 billion in share repurchases.

We remain confident in delivering durable margin expansion into FY2025, targeting 39%+ as 6G R&D and Open RAN scale.

As we dive into the details, I'd like to highlight one of the standout drivers of our results this quarter: our new product and service launches. These initiatives are central to our strategy of converging high-speed telecom infrastructure with premium media experiences, positioning us squarely against incumbents like Comcast's Xfinity and AT&T's converged bundles while capitalizing on the ongoing 5G and streaming wars.

In Q2, we rolled out three flagship offerings that leverage our nationwide 5G Standalone network—now covering 85% of the U.S. population with median download speeds of 650 Mbps—and our expanding fiber-to-the-home footprint, which hit 18.5 million homes passed, up 28% year-over-year. First, NexStream Ultra: Our low-latency, 5G-optimized streaming bundle integrating live sports, ad-supported video-on-demand, and premium SVOD content via exclusive partnerships with Peacock and Paramount+. Priced at $15/month standalone or bundled with mobile/postpaid plans for $10 add-on. Second, EdgeAI Connect: An enterprise-grade service using network slicing and multi-access edge computing for ultra-reliable, low-latency media delivery—think AR/VR concerts and cloud gaming for B2B clients like gaming studios and broadcasters. Third, FiberFusion Home: A gigabit symmetrical FTTH package bundled with our AI-driven content personalization engine, which uses machine learning to boost engagement by 30% based on viewing habits.

These aren't just bolt-ons; they're engineered on our Open RAN architecture, which reduced capex by 15% while enabling dynamic spectrum sharing for media prioritization during peak events like the Olympics.

Collectively, these launches generated $285 million in incremental revenue in Q2—representing 18% of our total service revenue of $1.58 billion, up 42% YoY from $200 million last year. NexStream Ultra drove $180 million, fueled by 65% take-rate among new postpaid mobile subscribers and a $3.50 ARPU uplift (now averaging $58/month for bundled customers). This outpaced industry averages, where ARPU erosion from cord-cutting persists at -2% for peers. EdgeAI Connect contributed $65 million from 450 new enterprise contracts, with 90-day payback periods thanks to 70% gross margins on edge services. FiberFusion Home added $40 million, with broadband revenue per account jumping 22% to $112/month.

Overall, these launches accelerated our wireless service revenue growth to 5.2% YoY (vs. flat industry) and fixed broadband to 12% YoY, helping deliver 360 bps of EBITDA margin expansion to 37.2%.

We're seeing explosive net adds: 1.8 million total new subscribers attributable to these launches in Q2, pushing our broadband/mobile converged base to 48.2 million—up 8% YoY and ahead of T-Mobile's postpaid momentum. NexStream Ultra added 1.1 million video subscribers, with quarterly churn dropping to 0.9% (vs. 1.8% industry for OTT bundles), driven by 4K/8K HDR streaming over 5G mmWave. EdgeAI Connect secured 12,000 enterprise seats, targeting the $15B edge media market projected by Gartner to grow 35% CAGR through 2028. FiberFusion Home delivered 650,000 broadband net adds, achieving 75% penetration in new FTTH markets—far surpassing Charter's 60% in comparable rural expansions.

Postpaid phone net adds hit 750,000, with 40% citing the media bundle as the primary driver, reversing the -1% subscriber erosion we saw in legacy plans.

Regionally: North America (85% of launch revenue) saw dominant performance in the U.S. Sunbelt markets, where 5G penetration exceeds 55% and FTTH competition from Google Fiber is fiercest; we gained 2% market share in video broadband per New Street Research, amid cord-nevers under 35 driving 25% of NexStream adds. Europe (10%) had early traction in the UK and Germany via our Vodafone partnership, adding 150,000 subs despite regulatory headwinds on spectrum auctions; EdgeAI is resonating with UEFA broadcasters needing sub-10ms latency. APAC/LATAM (5%, high-growth) added 200,000 in Brazil and India pilots, where affordable 5G bundles counter Jio's price wars—our ARPU holds at $25/month vs. their $10.

Key trend: The 'quad-play' convergence is winning, with 62% of new households opting for bundled mobile/fiber/video, up from 45% last year. We're bucking the 15% U.S. pay-TV subscriber decline per MoffettNathanson by embedding media into connectivity.

These launches validate our $2.5B 2024 capex plan, skewed 60% to 5G Advanced and fiber densification. We've locked in $500M in forward commitments from content deals like NBA rights extension and expect $1.1B in full-year incremental revenue from these ramps, implying 10-12% service revenue growth. Risks include OTT price hikes from Netflix (up 10% recently) and potential FCC net neutrality redux, but our vertically integrated edge gives us a moat.

We're ahead of the curve on 5G-6G media synergies, much like Verizon's YouTube TV pivot, and plan Q3 expansions into metaverse streaming pilots with Meta. This positions TeleWave for mid-teens EBITDA growth into 2025.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star then one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Morningstar. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the fiber buildout progress, especially take rates and how you're managing capex going forward?

Mike Thompson: Certainly, John. As Lisa detailed, our fiber program hit key milestones with 1.2 million incremental homes passed, reaching 18.5 million total, and we're seeing accelerating adoption at a 26% take rate, up to 28% in mature markets. This is driven by competitive pricing and bundling, with ARPU at $118. On capex, Q2 fiber spend was $1.1 billion, but we're guiding to $4.2-4.5 billion for the full year as we transition to maintenance. Regional expansions in the Northeast, Southeast, and Midwest are optimizing density for 30%+ take rates, and partnerships plus BEAD grants are keeping costs at $850 per passing. This builds our moat for multi-gig services and media delivery.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Davis with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Davis: Hi, thanks for taking my question. Could you elaborate on your plans for churn reduction and EBITDA margin guidance amid competitive pressures?

Lisa Chen: Yes, Emily. Our blended monthly churn improved to 1.12%, with segment wins in postpaid mobile at 0.85% and fixed broadband at 1.05%, thanks to network investments and AI retention tools achieving 92% churn prediction accuracy. Drivers like competitive poaching at 35% are offset by quad-play bundling at 65% penetration, cutting churn 30%. For EBITDA margins, Q2 hit 37.2%, and we're guiding Q3 to 36.5-38.0% and full-year 37.0-38.5%, driven by ARPU growth to $52.40, opex savings from SDN/NFV, and new launches adding $285 million. Cost controls and 5G Media Fusion will push us to 39%+ in 2025 despite energy and regulatory headwinds.

Sarah Johnson: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Mike, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Mike Thompson: Thank you. In closing, I am proud of our team's performance this quarter. We are well-positioned to continue delivering value to our customers and shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
